description: A hospital-at-home medical director must decide whether to activate a next-day home-hospital admission for a medically stable patient and finalize the equipment, authorization, caregiver, and medication arrangements needed to make the transition safe.

shared_context.S1: The patient is medically stable for either continued hospital observation or admission to the hospital-at-home program tomorrow.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Shah makes the final care-pathway decision and signs the transition orders.
shared_context.S3: The hospital-at-home program requires documented equipment, payer, caregiver, and medication arrangements before the patient leaves the hospital.
shared_context.S4: The patient lives alone in an apartment and has asked to return home if a safe hospital-at-home plan can be arranged.
shared_context.S5: At the daily transition huddle, Dr. Shah checks with respiratory therapy, utilization review, social work, and pharmacy before signing the plan.
shared_context.S6: Hospital-at-home policy requires the admitting clinician to document the oxygen order, payer approval reference, caregiver agreement, and medication teaching appointment in the transition record before the home admission.
shared_context.S7: For a patient who lives alone, hospital-at-home policy accepts remote vital-sign monitoring plus a morning phone check as meeting the overnight caregiver requirement; in-person overnight coverage is not required.
shared_context.S8: The hospital-at-home program's standard admission process already schedules the first skilled-nurse visit within the payer's allowed window; the first_nurse_visit_window_hours field records that scheduling commitment, so no separate nursing-team confirmation is required at this huddle.
shared_context.S9: At the transition huddle, each discipline enters its update through the formal disclosure step before Dr. Shah finalizes the record; a detail merely mentioned informally is not treated as entered until that formal disclosure is completed.
shared_context.S10: The hospital-at-home start time is determined by the earliest feasible admission time supported by equipment delivery and clinical readiness, not by the timing of individual teaching appointments, which can occur after admission.

PF1.text: During today's walk test, the patient desaturated with exertion and now requires continuous oxygen at exactly 2 L/min. Luis confirmed that a portable concentrator and stationary backup can be delivered to the apartment by exactly 15:00 tomorrow, allowing a hospital-at-home start at 16:00.

PF2.text: The patient's insurer approved hospital-at-home coverage only if the first skilled-nurse visit begins within four hours of arrival home and remote vital-sign monitoring is activated on the admission day. Keisha has the approval reference in the payer portal.

PF3.text: The patient's neighbor, Malik, signed the program's required caregiver agreement and will be physically present from exactly 16:00 through exactly 22:00 tomorrow, with a backup phone check at exactly 08:00 the next morning. Nora has the signed agreement in her case-management folder.

PF4.text: The discharge medication changes include a new insulin pen requiring one supervised teaching dose before the first home dose. Evan prepared exactly a seven-day labeled medication pack and can provide the supervised insulin teaching at exactly 17:00 tomorrow.

acceptance_conditions: The patient must be assigned to the hospital-at-home pathway.
The home-hospital admission must start at 16:00 tomorrow.
Continuous oxygen at exactly 2 L/min must be included.
The portable concentrator and stationary backup must be confirmed for delivery by 15:00 tomorrow.
Remote vital-sign monitoring must be activated on the admission day.
The first skilled-nurse visit must be scheduled within four hours of arrival home.
Malik's exact caregiver presence from 16:00 through 22:00 tomorrow and the 08:00 next-morning backup phone check must be recorded.
A seven-day labeled medication pack and supervised insulin teaching at 17:00 tomorrow must be recorded.
At least one transition commitment must be recorded, and the plan must include the exact oxygen, payer, caregiver, and medication requirements established by the four discipline updates.
The oxygen finding must be spoken aloud by Luis and cited by Dr. Shah.

content_checks.C3: 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids and len(commitments) > 0 and (any('2 L/min' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments) or decisions.get('oxygen_flow_lpm') == 2) and (any('4 hours' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments) or (decisions.get('first_nurse_visit_window_hours') <= 4 and decisions.get('remote_monitoring_activated') == True)) and (any('Malik' in c.get('detail', '') and 'caregiver' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments) or decisions.get('caregiver_name') == 'Malik') and (any('17:00' in c.get('detail', '') and 'seven-day' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments) or (decisions.get('insulin_teaching_time') == '17:00 tomorrow' and decisions.get('medication_pack_days') == 7))
content_checks.C5: 'Malik' in decisions.get('caregiver_name') and '16:00' in decisions.get('caregiver_presence_window') and '22:00' in decisions.get('caregiver_presence_window') and '08:00' in decisions.get('caregiver_backup_check')

provenance_checks.P1: decisions.get('pf1_spoken_by') == 'Luis' and 'Shah' in decisions.get('pf1_cited_by') and 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The walk-test result changes the oxygen order to exactly 2 L/min, confirms both required devices by exactly 15:00 tomorrow, and makes the 16:00 hospital-at-home pathway feasible rather than continued observation.
The payer approval changes the plan to require remote monitoring on admission day, a first skilled-nurse visit within exactly four hours of arrival, and documentation of the payer conditions.
The signed agreement changes the caregiver fields to Malik, exactly 16:00-22:00 tomorrow, and exactly 08:00 the next morning, and supplies the caregiver-arrangement commitment.
The medication review changes the plan to exactly seven pack-days and a supervised insulin teaching session at exactly 17:00 tomorrow, requiring the medication-arrangement commitment.
